item.text: I’m collecting a few direct confirmations on coordination mechanisms and the main counterweights, then I’ll stop and write the compact note with claim-level mapping only.

item.text:
**Assessment**  
Mostly yes, with important caveats. Marcos showed real top-down coordination and follow-through in 2024, especially in security, procurement, anti-poverty delivery, and economic management. The main weakness is that discipline still depended on a personalized ruling network and selective accountability, not fully impersonal institutions.

**Evidence For**
- **Executive Order No. 81** | Lawphil / Office of the President | December 30, 2024 | [URL](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_81_2024.html) | Reorganized the National Security Council to include the executive, legislative, military, intelligence, and legal sides in one coordination body, which is strong evidence of tighter security/institutional control and follow-through. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3
- **SONA Highlights Whole-of-Government Effort to Achieve Food Security, Inclusive Economic Growth-NEDA** | Presidential Communications Office / NEDA | July 23, 2024 | [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sona-highlights-whole-of-government-effort-to-achieve-food-security-inclusive-economic-growth-neda/) | Framed the SONA as an across-government implementation push for PDP 2023-2028, which is direct evidence of centralized agenda discipline. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.2, 8B.3
- **PBBM stands by suspension of 139 NFA officials** | Presidential Communications Office | March 6, 2024 | [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-stands-by-suspension-of-139-nfa-officials/) | Marcos backed mass suspensions after anomalous rice sales and procedural violations, showing he could enforce discipline inside a key implementing agency rather than sheltering it. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3
- **PBBM orders implementation of amnesty program to communist rebels** | Presidential Communications Office | April 4, 2024 | [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-implementation-of-amnesty-program-to-communist-rebels/) | Directed the NTF-ELCAC to implement the amnesty program and finalize IRR, a concrete example of using a formal security apparatus to push execution. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams** | Presidential Communications Office | July 20, 2024 | [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) | Standardized procurement and institutionalized e-procurement, which is direct evidence of process control, reporting discipline, and reduced discretion. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4
- **PBBM reorganizes NICA to ensure national security, promote national interest amid evolving threats** | Presidential Communications Office | January 23, 2024 | [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-reorganizes-nica-to-ensure-national-security-promote-national-interest-amid-evolving-threats/) | Reorganized intelligence collection and internal/external coordination, showing active attempt to tighten the security bureaucracy around a common operational line. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3
- **Marcos’s economic team public strategy forum** | Philippine News Agency | July 8, 2024 | [URL](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1228524) | Economic managers publicly coordinated inflation, growth, and investment policy across NEDA, BSP, DBM, Treasury, and the investment office, which is good evidence of technocratic coordination. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

**Evidence Against**
- **PFP, Lakas-CMD alliance under Alyansa Para sa Bagong Pilipinas a significant moment for PH politics, public service - PBBM** | Presidential Communications Office | May 8, 2024 | [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pfp-lakas-cmd-alliance-under-alyansa-para-sa-bagong-pilipinas-a-significant-moment-for-ph-politics-public-service-pbbm/) | The ruling coalition was being actively managed through party alliances tied to Marcos and Speaker Romualdez, which points to personalized coalition maintenance rather than purely institutional discipline. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **Marcos, Romualdez parties forge political alliance** | BusinessWorld Online | May 8, 2024 | [URL](https://www.bworldonline.com/the-nation/2024/05/08/593686/marcos-romualdez-parties-forge-political-alliance/) | The Marcos-Romualdez party alliance shows the ruling network remained fused to family strategy, which is a counterweight to a clean discipline-through-institutions reading. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **Philippines** | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | June 17, 2024 | [URL](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | The report says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and pressure over broadcasters persisted, suggesting the state’s control environment was still coercive and unevenly disciplined. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **Philippines | Freedom in the World 2024** | Freedom House | 2024 | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House says patronage, kinship, weak campaign-finance rules, and red-tagging continued, which indicates that follow-through and coordination still ran through transactional political structures. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- **No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it - PBBM** | Presidential Communications Office | November 14, 2024 | [URL](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/) | Marcos refused independent ICC cooperation, which is evidence that he would keep accountability and review tightly controlled when scrutiny reached politically sensitive territory. | QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4

**Search Gap**
- I did not find public internal scorecards, ministerial compliance reports, or party whip records that would show day-to-day discipline across regions and agencies.
- The strongest evidence is at the top of the system: cabinet, security, procurement, and coalition management. Evidence on lower-level implementation discipline is thinner and more indirect.
